observations.attribute: lesion location and interface with thoracic wall
observations.value: pleurally based mass abutting the chest wall with obtuse angles at the pleural interface, visible on PA CXR (Figure 1) and lateral CXR (Figure 2)
focal rib erosion adjacent to the mass, best seen on lateral CXR (Figure 2) and confirmed on CT (Figure 3)
well-circumscribed, lobulated soft-tissue mass without internal calcification; no pleural effusion
no evidence of endobronchial or central hilar mass; lesion is peripheral/pleural
no blunting of costophrenic angles or meniscus sign; no fluid collection
no intrinsic calcification within the lesion on CT (Figure 3)
Figure 1 and 2 are frontal and lateral chest radiographs (CXR); Figure 3 is axial CT slice through lower thorax

hypotheses.name: Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura (SFTP)
hypotheses.basis: Pleural-based, well-circumscribed mass with obtuse angles, rib erosion, and absence of calcification or effusion—classic imaging features of SFTP, especially when large and aggressive

hypotheses.name: Malignant pleural mesothelioma
hypotheses.basis: Less likely due to solitary, well-defined nature and lack of diffuse pleural thickening or effusion; however, localized forms can mimic SFTP

hypotheses.name: Metastatic pleural tumor
hypotheses.basis: Rib destruction raises concern for malignancy, but absence of multiple lesions or primary site makes metastasis less likely than primary pleural tumor
